definitions.explanation: A fire-resistant door installed in buildings to prevent the spread of fire and smoke between sections. Required by building codes in many structures.

examples.japanese: {防火扉|ぼうかとびら}は{常|つね}に{閉|し}めておいてください。
examples.english: Please keep the fire door closed at all times.

examples.japanese: {火災|かさい}が{発生|はっせい}すると、{防火扉|ぼうかとびら}が{自動的|じどうてき}に{閉|し}まる。
examples.english: When a fire breaks out, the fire doors close automatically.

examples.japanese: {避難訓練|ひなんくんれん}の{際|さい}、{防火扉|ぼうかとびら}の{前|まえ}に{物|もの}を{置|お}いてはいけないと{注意|ちゅうい}された。
examples.english: During the evacuation drill, we were warned not to place objects in front of the fire doors.

notes:
A compound of {防火|ぼうか} (fire prevention/fireproofing) + {扉|とびら} (door). Found in apartment buildings, offices, schools, and commercial buildings throughout Japan. Japanese building codes ({建築基準法|けんちくきじゅんほう}) require fire doors in structures above a certain size.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {防火扉|ぼうかとびら}を{閉|し}める: to close the fire door
- {防火扉|ぼうかとびら}が{作動|さどう}する: the fire door activates
- {防火扉|ぼうかとびら}の{点検|てんけん}: fire door inspection
- {防火扉|ぼうかとびら}の{前|まえ}: in front of the fire door

RELATED WORDS:
- {防火|ぼうか}: fire prevention; fireproofing
- {防火壁|ぼうかへき}: firewall (physical wall in a building)
- {非常口|ひじょうぐち}: emergency exit
- {避難経路|ひなんけいろ}: evacuation route
